ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a transition-state structure inside parentheses, and there are electron-flow curved arrows; the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Looking at the structure from left to right, the left end has an Ar group connected to a vinylic carbon, and this carbon forms a double-bond fragment with a positively charged oxygen; this positively charged oxygen continues to connect to a methylene, followed by a carbonyl C(=O), and then to a central carbon. The central carbon is marked with H above and is connected to Ru(Por) below. The right side of the central carbon is connected to another carbonyl C(=O), then connected to an OR¹ ester group. Then reason: According to the method draft, represent Ar with the wildcard *; write the left-end vinylic/oxonium fragment as *C=[O+]; continue along the main chain as [O+]CC(=O)C; the central carbon is connected to Ru(Por), represented with a wildcard branch as C(*); the right-end ester group is written as C(=O)O*. Combining gives SMILES: *C=[O+]CC(=O)C(*)C(=O)O*.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Read the chemical skeleton in the image from left to right, excluding the electron-flow arrows as instructed. Convert the Ar group to a leading wildcard `*` attached to the alkene carbon, encode the alkene/oxonium fragment as `*C=[O+]`, then continue along the chain as `[O+]C C(=O) C(...) C(=O) O...`. Add the Ru(Por) group on the central carbon as a wildcard branch `C(*)`, and add the ester R1 group after oxygen as `O*`. Combine these pieces into the SMILES `*C=[O+]CC(=O)C(*)C(=O)O*`.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中是一个括号内的过渡态结构，并有电子流曲箭头；题目要求忽略这些箭头。结构从左到右看，左端有 Ar 基团连接到一个烯基碳，该碳与带正电的氧形成双键片段；这个带正电的氧继续连到一个亚甲基，随后是一个羰基 C(=O)，再到一个中心碳。中心碳上方标有 H，下方连有 Ru(Por)。中心碳右侧接另一个羰基 C(=O)，再连到 OR¹ 酯基。再推理：按方法草案，将 Ar 用通配符 * 表示，左端烯基/氧鎓片段写作 *C=[O+]；继续沿主链写为 [O+]CC(=O)C；中心碳连接 Ru(Por)，用通配符支链表示为 C(*)；右端酯基写作 C(=O)O*。合并得到 SMILES：*C=[O+]CC(=O)C(*)C(=O)O*。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct visual-to-SMILES transcription is the natural single route for this problem; it is distinct in focusing on reading the drawn connectivity left-to-right while treating all generic substituent labels as wildcard atoms.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the bracketed transition-state drawing: identify the left Ar substituent attached to an alkene carbon, the double bond to a positively charged oxygen, the O–CH2–C(=O)–C(H)(Ru(Por))–C(=O)–OR1 chain, and ignore all curved arrows and brackets.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the requested output is a SMILES expression and that arrows should be ignored; no other text data are needed.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES rules: generic groups Ar, Ru(Por), and R1 can be represented by wildcard atoms `*`; charged oxonium must be bracketed as `[O+]`; carbonyls are `C(=O)`; branches encode substituents such as `C(*)`; implicit hydrogens need not be written.
